drhp.business: The Grob Tea Company Limited cultivates, manufactures and sells tea from its tea estates in Assam and Cachar, North-East India, producing predominantly CTC tea (Assam CTC and Cachar CTC) with a growing Orthodox tea line, sold into domestic and export markets. The company employs over 3,781 people across its tea estates and other establishments.
drhp.expansion: The company commissioned a new Orthodox tea factory at Kanu T.E., which went into production from July 2025 and produced 2.74 lac kgs of Orthodox tea in FY26. It is now building a second Orthodox tea factory at Pathemara T.E. (Cachar), with capacity to produce 10.00 lac kgs of Orthodox tea annually; construction is ongoing and production is expected to begin by end of August 2026, diversifying the company's product mix and enabling it to explore new markets for Cachar produce.

litigation.note: No material litigation disclosed in the annual report.

risks.note: Tea crop is entirely rain-dependent; erratic climate change with very high ambient temperature and erratic rainfall patterns (long dry spells punctuated by heavy short rain) is flagged as frequently jeopardising production across all tea-growing regions, particularly the North-East.

Tea being a labour-intensive industry, shortage of labour during peak season plus a substantial increase in labour, social and other input costs is flagged as the major structural cause of concern for the industry.

Average sale price realization fell across Assam CTC (-7.70%), Cachar and Orthodox varieties in FY26 due to the supply-demand mechanism of the market, directly driving the fall in the Company's profitability during the year.
Import of cheap varieties of tea getting mixed with domestic production is flagged by management as a matter of serious concern for market stability.
risks.risk: Cheap tea imports diluting the domestic market

risks.note: Incumbent statutory auditor M/s GARV & Associates resigned effective 13th May, 2026, immediately after issuing the FY26 audit report; M/s B Nath & Company was appointed to fill the casual vacancy, subject to shareholder ratification/approval at the ensuing AGM.

The FY2024-25 secretarial audit flagged incomplete/delayed disclosure to stock exchanges around a Company Secretary's resignation, and a non-compliance under SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulation 9 concerning disclosure by an immediate relative of a designated person; remedial clarifications/responses were filed with the exchanges.
